newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end lower on negative rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end lower on negative rumours.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed down on Friday, dragged down by speculation that bad news will emerge after the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on July 1, brokers said.

The B index was dragged down by a sharp decline in the A share market, which was hit by rumours the government plans to allow part of China's government and institutional shares, which are not traded, to list on the stock market, they said.
The B index fell 0.651 points or 0.79 percent to 81.478 points on volume of 19.669 million shares worth $10.845 million, compared with around $16.4 million on Thursday.
Similar rumours that state shares and legal person shares generated from rights offers would be listed have circulated in the markets previously.
Speaking from Beijing, an official of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the market watchdog, denied knowledge of any pending announcement on the matter.
The rumours affected the A index more strongly than the B shares, which were calmer ahead of a two-day market holiday next week for the Hong Kong handover, brokers said.

"The (B share) market was relatively quiet today as it is the final trading day ahead of the Hong Kong handover and investors are reluctant to trade with a holiday approaching," one local broker said.
The British colony of Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30. The Shanghai Stock Exchange will be closed for a holiday on Monday and Tuesday for the event.

"The major positive factor (the Hong Kong handover) which boosted the market for half a year has faded, and technical charts showed a weak short-term outlook, resulting in today's falls," the local broker said.
Of 45 B shares, 42 traded with 25 down, 14 up and three flat.
B share companies expected to report poor interim results for the first half of 1997 in July and August rounded out the list of the sharpest losers on Friday, brokers said.
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass Co. was the biggest loser, plunging $0.040 or 9.95 percent to $0.362 on volume of 126,000 shares.
Newcomer Hainan Airlines Co Ltd, which listed on Thursday, was the most actively traded B share, rising $0.010 or 1.87 percent to $0.546 on volume of around 5.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index plunged 36.421 points or 2.71 percent to 1,306.778 points on volume of 530.587 million shares worth 8.3 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index ended down 71.086 points or 1.72 percent at 4,066.581 points.
Precision Alloy Co was the biggest A share loser on profit-taking. It plunged 0.86 yuan or 10.02 percent to 7.72 yuan.
Brokers said the A and B share markets will likely consolidate lower next week following the holiday as investors await fresh leads.
